description: The plot shows how “Similarity” of Hidden State Alignments varies across model layers for four language pairs (en&en, en&es, en&el, en&bn). The x-axis is labeled “Layer” on a linear scale, spanning 0 to 22 with tick labels every 2 layers. The y-axis is labeled “Similarity” on a linear scale, ranging from 0.00 to 0.45 with tick labels every 0.05. Four solid lines without markers are shown: en&en is a dark red line that starts near 0.07 at layer 0, rises to about 0.10 by layer 2, climbs to a local maximum around 0.26 at layer 6, drops to roughly 0.16 at layer 7–9, stays around ~0.17–0.18 near layers 10–12, declines to about 0.12–0.13 around layers 15–16, dips to roughly 0.08–0.10 around layers 18–21, then rises sharply to about 0.43 at layer 22. en&es is a blue line that begins near 0.06 at layer 0, increases to about 0.09–0.10 by layers 2–3, peaks near 0.24 at layer 6, drops to about 0.15 around layers 7–9, sits near ~0.17–0.18 around layers 10–12, declines to about 0.11–0.12 around layers 15–16, falls to roughly 0.05–0.07 around layers 19–21, and then increases to about 0.27 at layer 22. en&el is a green line that starts near 0.04 at layer 0, rises to about 0.08 at layer 2, reaches about 0.15 at layer 6, drops to around 0.10 at layer 7, increases gradually to about 0.14–0.15 around layers 12–13, declines to roughly 0.09 around layers 15–16, reaches about 0.05 around layers 19–21, and then rises to about 0.30 at layer 22. en&bn is a pink line that begins near 0.03–0.04 at layer 0, rises to about 0.07 at layer 2, reaches about 0.14 at layer 6, drops to around 0.09–0.10 at layer 7, increases to about 0.13–0.14 around layers 12–13, declines to roughly 0.08–0.09 around layers 15–16, falls to about 0.05–0.06 around layers 19–21, and then increases to about 0.29–0.30 at layer 22.
caption_used: This line plot illustrates the similarity of Hidden State Alignments (HSAs) across different language pairs within the Qwen1.5-1.8B model, evaluated across all layers. The horizontal axis, labeled 'Layer,' spans from 0 to 22 in increments of 2, while the vertical axis, labeled 'Similarity,' ranges from 0.00 to 0.45 in increments of 0.05. Four language pairs are depicted: English-English (en&en, red), English-Spanish (en&es, blue), English-Greek (en&el, green), and English-Bengali (en&bn, pink). The en&en pair demonstrates a pronounced peak at layer 6, reaching a similarity of approximately 0.26, before stabilizing around 0.15 from layers 8 to 18 and sharply rising to 0.43 at layer 22. The en&es pair follows a similar trajectory, peaking at 0.24 at layer 6, but subsequently declines more gradually, maintaining a similarity of roughly 0.12 between layers 10 and 16, and ultimately rising to 0.27 at layer 22. The en&el pair exhibits a modest peak of 0.15 at layer 6, then collapses to near-baseline levels by layer 10, remaining stagnant until a late resurgence to 0.18 at layer 22. The en&bn pair, while initially the lowest, consistently surpasses the en&el pair after layer 8, achieving a final similarity of 0.30 at layer 22. Notably, the en&es pair consistently exceeds the en&el pair in similarity across all intermediate layers, underscoring a robust cross-linguistic alignment for high-resource languages.
